questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a qualitative demand / ? , , ] a). Time-series b). The Delphi c). Exponential d). Regression analysis Method smoothing analysis
questions.solution_html:
• b
  • Advertising
  • Relationship Marketing – building long-term relationships with stakeholders.
  • Idea Generation
  • Demographic Segmentation – age, gender, income, education, etc.
  • Exploratory Research Design
  • Used to explore or gain insights into a problem.
  • Helps identify new ideas or relationships.
  • Usually qualitative in nature (e.g., interviews, focus groups).
  • Example: Interviewing fans to understand reasons for declining match attendance.
  • Building Long-Term Customer Loyalty
  • Relationship marketing helps a fitness studio retain members by maintaining strong personal
  • connections, offering customized workout plans, and recognizing loyal customers.
  • Defining the Problem
  • Samsung wants to understand consumer preferences for battery life, camera quality, and
  • price expectations before launching the new phone.
  • Meaning
  • Consumer Market: Buyers purchase goods and services for personal use.
  • Business Market: Buyers purchase goods and services for resale or production purposes.
  • Consistent Branding
  • Ensures that all promotional messages—on TV, social media, print, and outdoor
  • ads—deliver the same brand image.
  • Targeted Marketing
  • Allows the brand to focus on specific groups (e.g., youth athletes, casual wearers, or
  • professionals).
  • Global Brand Presence
  • Sports brands like Adidas, Puma, and Nike operate and sell in multiple countries.
questions.final_answer: Sports brands like Adidas, Puma, and Nike operate and sell in multiple countries
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: A company segments its market based on age, gender, and income. / This is an example of which type of segmentation? a). Psychographic b). Demographic c). Behavioral d). Geographic
questions.solution_html:
• b
  • Sales Promotion
  • Integrated Marketing – ensuring consistency across all marketing activities.
  • Idea Screening
  • Psychographic Segmentation – lifestyle, values, personality.
  • Descriptive Research Design
  • Describes characteristics of a population or phenomenon.
  • Quantitative in nature (e.g., surveys, observation).
  • Answers questions like “who,” “what,” “when,” and “where.”
  • Example: Survey to find out the percentage of fans who buy tickets online.
  • Personalized Communication
  • Through regular follow-ups, fitness progress tracking, and personalized messages, members
  • feel valued and motivated to continue.
  • Developing the Research Plan
  • Decide on data sources (primary and secondary), sampling methods, and research tools
  • such as surveys, interviews, and focus groups.
  • Type of Buyer
  • Consumer Market: Individuals and households.
  • Business Market: Organizations, institutions, and companies.
  • Wider Reach
  • Different media channels reach different audience segments (youth via Instagram, families
  • via TV, etc.).
  • Product Customization
  • Different segments need different products — e.g., high-performance shoes for athletes
  • stylish sneakers for youth.
  • Standardized Products
  • Same sports goods are available globally, creating a universal market.
questions.final_answer: Same sports goods are available globally, creating a universal market
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: A company launches a new product with high promotional spending and / . Which PLC stage does this , , ] strategy describe? a). b). Introduction Decline c). d). Growth Maturity
questions.solution_html:
• b
  • Public Relations/Publicity
  • Internal Marketing – motivating and training employees for customer satisfaction.

  • Behavioral Segmentation – usage rate, brand loyalty, benefits sought.

  • Conduct online surveys with potential customers, analyze competitors’ phones, and gather
  • sales data from dealers.

  • Business Market: Large or bulk quantities.
  • Enhanced Engagement
  • Social media interaction, contests, and live updates create excitement and audience
  • participation.

questions.question: What are the repeat order and modified repeat in business market
questions.solution_html:
• Repeat Order: When a buyer purchases the same product from the same supplier without
  • any changes in specifications, price, or terms. It is also known as a straight rebuy.
  • Modified Repeat (Modified Rebuy): When the buyer wants to change product specifications
  • price, delivery schedule, or supplier due to changed needs or dissatisfaction.
